text:
sam_support: ACME (acme_pm) reports ~10% 504s from hosted /v1/generate between 2026-03-05T14:23Z-14:37Z. SDK retries causing billing spike. Customer attached request-id: r-9b1c4f. Can we triage?

anya_sre: on it. Any repro steps / curl + request-id sample plz. Also any spikes in deploys? @deploy-bot any deploys around 14:20-14:30Z?

acme_pm: here's minimal repro we ran from their infra:

curl -i -X POST "https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  -H "X-Request-ID: r-9b1c4f" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-7b","input":"short prompt","max_tokens":64}'

Response: HTTP/1.1 504 Gateway Timeout after ~30s

They also saw retry loop in our SDK (p95 retries ~3)

sam_support: thanks, attaching customer's timing and logs.

deploy-bot: release/redwood-runtime v2.14.7 promoted to prod @ 2026-03-05T14:18:02Z (binaries: batch-window tweak)

marco_eng: flagging possible correlation with the runtime change (batch_window_ms reduced) — could cause many small micro-requests to be dispatched, increasing K/V cache lock contention. Also watch auth cache misses if token refreshs spiked.

anya_sre: ran quick grep on ingress logs for r-9b1c4f, found upstream msg:

"[upstream] request-id=r-9b1c4f status=504 backend_err='kvcache-lock-timeout' wait_ms=30504"

anya_sre: looks like kv cache lock wait >30s then timeout. Need heap of kvcache metrics and lock contention. @marco_eng can you confirm change touched kvcache routing?

marco_eng: yes, v2.14.7 tightened prefix batching and changed lock backoff. Reverting to previous backoff is low-risk mitigation. Also propose temporary per-customer rate cap + fallback to redwood-3b to reduce token pressure.

taylan_oncall: I've applied a soft rate-cap for acme_pm (20rps) and enabled fallback route to redwood-3b for the customer. Watching.

sam_support: draft customer message for review:

"Hi ACME — we saw intermittent 504s from our hosted inference API earlier today (14:23–14:37 UTC). Root cause appears to be a runtime configuration change that increased lock contention on our K/V prefix cache, causing upstream timeouts. We've applied temporary rate limits and rolled back the change for affected nodes. You should see stability now; we will monitor for 2 hours and follow up with a post-incident summary. Apologies for the disruption. — Sam"

anya_sre: please add note about billing — we'll issue credit for retry-related tokens while we adjudicate.

acme_pm: thanks — they're seeing reduction already. we'll keep monitoring. :thumbsup:
